title: Choosing a University Major Before Friday
script: Dewi: [worried] Rio, I have to choose my university major by Friday, and I honestly still have no idea what to pick.
Rio: [calmly] Okay, don't panic yet. What subjects have you actually enjoyed the most these past few years?
Dewi: [thoughtful] I've always liked biology, but everyone keeps telling me medicine takes too many years and too much money.
Rio: [gently] That's true for medicine specifically, but biology leads to other paths too, like research or environmental science.
Dewi: [curious] I never really considered those options. Why didn't anyone mention them to me before?
Rio: [honestly] Because medicine and engineering get mentioned constantly, while quieter fields rarely get discussed at family dinners.
Dewi: [worried] What if I choose something and then discover later that I hate it after two years of studying?
Rio: [reassuring] That happens to plenty of people, and most universities allow you to change your path if it truly isn't working.
Dewi: [considering] That's somewhat comforting, although I still feel pressure to choose perfectly on the very first try.
Rio: [warmly] Nobody chooses perfectly the first time, Dewi. I certainly didn't, and I changed my major during my second year.
Dewi: [surprised] Wait, I didn't know that. You always seem so confident about your career now.
Rio: [laughing softly] I wasn't confident then. I was confused and scared, exactly like you sound right now.
Dewi: [thoughtful] Okay, that actually helps. I think I'll research environmental science programs before Friday's deadline.
Rio: [encouraging] Good idea. Talk to a few students already in that program too, if you can find any this week.
Dewi: [determined] I will. Thank you for not just telling me to pick medicine like everyone else does.
Rio: [warmly] That's what older brothers are for, apparently. Call me again once you've decided, and good luck researching tonight.
Dewi: [relieved] I will. Thanks, Rio. I feel calmer already, just from talking this through with you.
